The main takeaway from our work is that
metasomatic processes in magmatic-hydro-thermal systems can be studied by integrating field observations, mineral chemistry, and thermodynamic modeling.

the granite–carbonate system represents a unique natural laboratory to study metasomatic processes in a time-transgressive fashion, and to investigate element mobility and mineralization during magmatic–metasomatic processes.

the metasomatic front is a key feature to understand the evolution of a magmatic-hydrothermally driven system, as it is the locus where the most important exchange of major and minor/trace elements occurs.
